name: Tanzania Peaberry, Kilimanjaro and Arusha
origin: Tanzania, Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions (smallholder blend)
process: Fully washed: hand-pulped, bucket-fermented, dried on raised beds
vendor_notes: Juicy, smooth medium-to-full body with crisp, bright, tangy winey acidity; fruity and winey. Brightness 6/7, body 5/7, sweetness 7/7. Grown 1,100-1,700 m.
goal: Light roast for espresso: tangy, winey fruit with juicy sweetness
rationale: Washed East African peaberry: small, round, dense beans that tumble evenly and take heat efficiently, so they get a firm but slightly gentler charge than the Limu (190 C vs 195 C) to avoid tipping the rounded surface. The lot's appeal is bright, winey acidity and a very high sweetness rating (7/7), so a light roast can stay short after first crack without going sour: ~9.5 C after FC, DTR ~18%. FC 188 C follows the washed coffees on this roaster; peaberries often crack early and loudly, so mark FC at the first clear pops. If shots are sour or thin, add 10-15 s of development first.
steps: Preheat to 190 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 190. Burner 73%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 111 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 178 C (~6:06): burner 46%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:15 at ~188 C: burner 41%, air 50. Then 36%.
Drop ~8:50 at ~197.5 C (9.5 C after FC).

rest.note: Light, dense washed peaberry degasses slowly. Give it at least 8 days; the winey fruit and sweetness come together around day 12.

history.note: Initial light-roast espresso plan from the Coffee Bean Corral listing, using the measured opening on this roaster (TP ~0:36 at ~110 C) and FC 187-189 C from the washed coffees roasted so far.
